title: From Certifying Rank $k$ Projectors To Non-Positivity, Entanglement, And Non-Hermitian Witnesses Through Traces Of Matrix Powers
abstract: We all know that a density matrix $ρ$ is pure if and only if $\mathrm{Tr} \,ρ^2 = 1$. But is this the only way to prove the purity of $ρ$ using the trace of its powers? Here I systematically study the necessary and sufficient conditions of the more general question of guaranteeing that all eigenvalues of a Hermitian matrix belong to a specified set through its trace of powers. More importantly, these characterization results are automatically witnesses certifying a quantum state as entangled, a Hermitian operator has least one negative eigenvalue and a linear operator as non-Hermitian. I demonstrate the effectiveness of these witnesses, analyze their performance, and study their strength, weakness together with resource requirement through numerical simulation as well as analytical work. I also discuss briefly the effects of numerical stability, uncertainty in measurement and rounding errors on these problems.
summary: This paper develops a general mathematical framework to test spectral properties of quantum operators using only the traces of their powers. It establishes various 'witnesses' derived from these traces that can certify crucial quantum features like entanglement or non-positivity. This provides a powerful, resource-efficient diagnostic tool for quantum state characterization.
main_problem: The paper systematically studies necessary and sufficient conditions to constrain the eigenvalues of Hermitian matrices using the traces of their powers.
main_result: These trace-based conditions serve as powerful witnesses to certify quantum state properties, such as entanglement, non-positivity, and non-Hermiticity.
method: The core method involves deriving and analyzing polynomial inequalities involving $	ext{Tr} H^j$ to place constraints on the spectrum of the matrix $H$.
model_or_system: The analysis focuses on Hermitian matrices ($H$) and density matrices ($ho$) relevant to quantum information theory. The results generalize the purity condition ($	ext{Tr} ho^2 = 1$) to broader spectral constraints.
key_observables: The primary observables are the traces of matrix powers ($	ext{Tr} H^j$), which are used to diagnose properties like purity, rank, non-negativity, and Hermiticity.
important_parameters: The analysis considers the dimension of the matrix ($	ext{dim } H$), the number of distinct eigenvalues ($p$), and the impact of measurement uncertainty ($\delta$) and machine epsilon ($u$).
main_assumptions: The authors address limitations regarding the number of traces needed to determine the spectrum and the practical challenges posed by numerical stability and measurement errors.
figures_summary: The notes mention tables (Table II, III, IV) summarizing the performance of various witnesses (UTNPW, NPW, EW) for certifying non-positivity and entanglement across different dimensions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from generalizing the purity condition to establishing general theorems (Theorem 1) for eigenvalue constraints, then developing specific witnesses (NHW, UTNPW, NPW, EW) for physical properties, and concluding with a discussion of performance and open questions.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, purely algebraic tools derived from moment calculations to diagnose fundamental quantum properties (like entanglement or non-negativity) without requiring full knowledge of the Hamiltonian or state preparation.
